description: From the defk-fr7 stress runs (2026-10-11): at load above ~100 on the 12-core M4, ScaledFactsTest 'a dropped bounds check is never wrong' and 'a dropped overflow check is never wrong' failed every run with ExUnit's default 60 s per-test timeout, and BinaryLiteralsTest 'other segments are rejected' hit it once. All pass alone. Find why these tests take tens of seconds (kernel compiles per property case? clang per case?), make them cheaper (compile once, fewer runs in the default suite and the long form under :deep), or give them an explicit @tag timeout with a reason. Done when they finish well under the limit at load ~100, and the default suite time doesn't grow.

comments.text: Cause: pure CPU, no clang. Each of the 4000 cases per property runs Defk.Compiler.compile (~0.44 ms) plus ~100-length arithmetic checks: bounds 2.1 s, overflow 4.3 s idle; under 12 busy 'yes' loops overflow took 61.7 s (bounds 26.9 s), reproducing the timeout. Fix: default suite 500 cases each (idle 0.27 s / 0.53 s; under 12 yes loops 7.9 s / 6.5 s), the original 4000 cases kept as '(deep)' twins (@tag :deep, timeout 600 s; idle 2.2 s / 4.4 s). BinaryLiteralsTest 'other segments are rejected' is 8 small Code.compile_file calls, 46 ms idle, 1.2 s under load; cannot be tuned further, the one 60 s hit was a stall under load > 100 that I could not reproduce. Slowest tests left (not same shape, not fixed): ElixirModeTest Mix.install script 24-30 s, LanguageDocExamplesTest BEAM-of-their-own 5-17 s, DocsChecksTest links 5 s, NoConflictMarkersTest 3 s, AllocZeroTest K.in_loop 2.5 s.

title: Slow property tests hit ExUnit's 60 s timeout when the machine is loaded
